concepts.def: Assembly of three estates summoned by Louis XVI to address France's fiscal crisis, last met in 1614, sparking the revolution when the Third Estate broke away.

concepts.term: Declaration of the Rights of Man 1789
concepts.def: Foundational text of August 1789 proclaiming liberty, equality and popular sovereignty, dismantling the privileges of the old regime.
Period of mass executions directed by Robespierre's Committee of Public Safety against suspected enemies of the revolution, ending with his fall.

Napoleon Bonaparte's seizure of power in November 1799 that overthrew the Directory and established the Consulate, ending the revolutionary republic.

walkthroughs.body_html:
France in Revolution 1774-1815 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

France in Revolution 1774-1815 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with France in Revolution 1774-1815.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What body did Louis XVI summon in 1789 to solve the financial crisis?
options: The Estates-General
The National Assembly
The Convention
The Directory

mcqs.q: What event of 14 July 1789 symbolised the popular revolution?
options: The Storming of the Bastille
The Tennis Court Oath
The execution of the king
The fall of Robespierre

mcqs.q: Who dominated the Committee of Public Safety during the Terror?
options: Robespierre
Danton
Lafayette
Mirabeau

mcqs.q: How did Napoleon Bonaparte come to power in 1799?
options: By a coup overthrowing the Directory
By winning a national election
By inheriting the throne
By a vote of the Estates-General

mcqs.q: What did the Storming of the Bastille achieve militarily in 1789?
options: Napoleon restored the Bourbon monarchy in 1799.
The Bastille was Louis XVI's main palace.
The Bastille was a vast prison freed of thousands of political prisoners.
Little militarily — the fortress held only seven prisoners — but it was a hugely powerful symbolic blow against royal authority.

mcqs.q: Who held power during the Terror of 1793-94?
options: The Committee of Public Safety, dominated by Robespierre, directed the Terror, not the king, who had already been executed in January 1793.
Napoleon restored the Bourbon monarchy in 1799.
Louis XVI ordered the executions of the Terror.
Napoleon ran the Terror before becoming emperor.

mcqs.q: Was Napoleon's 1799 rise a continuation of the revolution?
options: The Bastille was Louis XVI's main palace.
Napoleon was elected by the French people to lead the republic.
Napoleon ended the revolutionary republic by seizing power in a coup, though he preserved some revolutionary reforms like legal equality.
Napoleon restored the Bourbon monarchy in 1799.
